text: The Constitution created an executive department that provided such a check. A person elected to that high office, with constituents in every section, state, and subdivision of the Union, must consider himself bound by the most solemn obligations to guard, protect, and defend the rights of all and of every portion, great or small, from the injustice and oppression of the rest. I therefore consider the veto power given by the Constitution to the Executive of the United States solely as a conservative power, to be used only: first, to protect the Constitution from violation; second, to protect the people from the effects of hasty legislation where their will has probably been disregarded or not well understood; and third, to prevent the effects of combinations that violate the rights of minorities.
